results.title: Louer une A100 à l'heure : prix comparés et quand elle suffit
results.author: Benoit Gouthière
highlights:
La réponse courte : une A100 de 80 Go fait tourner la plupart des modèles d’image, de vidéo et de langage qu’on sert en 2026, pour environ la moitié du prix d’une H100. Le 27 septembre 2026, elle se louait de 0,43 $ de l’heure chez l’hôte le moins cher de Vast.ai à plus de 5 $ chez Google Cloud, avec un cœur de marché entre 1,20 $ et 1,80 $. La H100 ne devient indispensable que pour l’entraînement de gros modèles, le calcul en FP8 ou les services qui ont besoin de chaque milliseconde. C’est la question la plus rentable des comparaisons entre fournisseurs GPU, parce qu’elle revient à se demander si l’on paie la carte dont on a besoin ou celle dont on parle.

L’A100, de génération Ampere, existe en 40 et en 80 Go, en format PCIe ou SXM, selon la fiche officielle de NVIDIA. La version de 80 Go a la même mémoire qu’une H100 : tout modèle qui tient dans l’une tient dans l’autre. La H100, de génération Hopper, calcule plus vite et gère nativement le format FP8, que l’A100 ignore. Pour de l’inférence de modèles de diffusion ou de LLM quantifiés, cette avance se paie souvent plus qu’elle ne rapporte.

> Pour qui : un développeur ou une équipe qui fait de l’inférence ou du fine-tuning sur des modèles qui tiennent en 80 Go, et veut payer la carte la plus rentable.
> 
> À partir de : 1,19 $ de l’heure pour une A100 PCIe de 80 Go en Community Cloud, 1,79 $ en Secure Cloud (relevé le 29 octobre 2026), facturés à la seconde.
> 
> Pour démarrer : ouvrir un compte Runpod, lancer le même travail sur une A100 puis sur une H100, et comparer le coût par tâche plutôt que le prix de l’heure.

results.title: Verda explained: GPU cloud, serverless and pricing
results.author: Sequenced desk
highlights:
Verda brings several ways of running AI workloads into one GPU cloud: individual instances, multi-node clusters and serverless containers. The company previously operated as DataCrunch. Its current offer is most useful when a team needs to move between experimentation, training and deployment without pretending those workloads have identical storage, latency or billing requirements.

...

## 01 / Product One company identity, several execution models

Verda’s rebrand announcement describes the transition from DataCrunch to Verda as a change of name with the same company, team and platform. The announcement set the website transition for November 2025. Older DataCrunch references therefore belong to this company history rather than a separate competing provider.

...

## 04 / Pricing The same GPU name can carry a different service price

The public pricing page separates GPU instances from serverless configurations. The entries below are USD figures consulted on 23 September 2026. CPU, memory and deployment arrangements differ between services, so the H100 rows are not interchangeable quotations for an identical bundle.

results.title: Cheapest A100 Rental: 40GB vs 80GB Prices by Provider · Aliteq
results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
On Nov 12, 2026 a 40GB A100 rented from $0.32/hr on Vast.ai and an 80GB one from $0.81/hr (Lium; Vast from $0.84), against $1.35 on Hyperstack (Nov 3) and $1.79 on Runpod. Where the cheap A100s are, why 80GB costs about twice as much, and the jobs that need it.

...

The cheapest A100 rental is on Vast.ai's marketplace, and the memory size changes the price. In our read of Vast's offer API at 13:30 UTC on Nov 3, 2026, a 40GB A100 started at $0.40/hour on-demand (median $0.53 across 39 offers) and an 80GB A100 at $0.63/hour (median $1.00 across 25 offers). The cheapest 80GB card from a Vast-verified host was $1.00. Managed 80GB A100s listed at $1.35 on Hyperstack and $1.79 on Runpod Secure Cloud. Pay for 80GB when you run a 70B model, gpt-oss-120b or a 70B fine-tune; for 32B-class models and smaller fine-tunes, 40GB does the job for about half the price. Prices move every hour, so check today's live prices before you rent.

## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

The cheapest A100 rental on November 3, 2026 was on Vast.ai's marketplace: an A100 40GB from $0.40 an hour on-demand (median $0.53) and an A100 80GB from $0.63 an hour (median $1.00 across 25 offers; the cheapest from a verified host was $1.00). Managed 80GB A100s listed at $1.35 an hour on Hyperstack and $1.79 on Runpod Secure Cloud. Lambda and CoreWeave sell 80GB A100s only in 8-GPU machines, at $2.79 and $2.70 per GPU-hour. The 80GB card is worth its roughly double price when the job needs more than 40GB: Llama 3.3 70B at 4-bit (about 43 GB at 8K context by our estimate), gpt-oss-120b (OpenAI says it runs on a single 80GB GPU), QLoRA fine-tuning of a 70B model (41 GB per Unsloth) or 16-bit LoRA of a 32B model (76 GB). For 32B models at 8-bit with short context, or QLoRA up to about 40B, a 40GB A100 is enough.

results.title: GPU cloud Europe 2026 : panorama des fournisseurs et tarifs
results.author: Benoit Gouthière
highlights:
La réponse courte : huit fournisseurs établis en Europe louent des GPU en 2026, avec des profils très différents. OVHcloud et Scaleway couvrent l’essentiel à des prix proches des néo-clouds américains. Infomaniak, en Suisse, affiche l’A100 et la L40S les moins chères du relevé, à condition de demander l’accès. Nebius et Verda louent des H100 depuis la Finlande, Outscale vise les administrations avec une offre qualifiée SecNumCloud. C’est la plus large des comparaisons entre plateformes GPU de ce guide, et la seule où chaque ligne a un drapeau différent.

Un mot sur la méthode. Les prix sont hors taxes et relevés le 27 septembre 2026 sur les grilles officielles. Ils ne se comparent pas tous directement : Outscale facture la carte seule, le processeur et la mémoire à part, alors qu’ Infomaniak et Verda facturent une instance complète. Deux noms souvent cités manquent volontairement. Hyperstack, dont le siège est à Londres, héberge ses GPU haut de gamme au Québec, selon sa propre documentation. Genesis Cloud, basé à Munich, n’avait plus de site accessible le jour du relevé.

> Pour qui : une équipe qui veut ses données en Suisse, une A100 ou une L40S facturée en euros, et une infrastructure exploitée entièrement hors de l’Union comme des États-Unis.
> 
> À partir de : 0,63 € hors taxes de l’heure pour une instance L40S, 1,31 € pour une A100 de 80 Go, et 300 CHF de crédit d’essai à utiliser sur trois mois.
> 
> Pour démarrer : ouvrir le Public Cloud Infomaniak, puis demander au support l’activation des GPU sur le projet.

| Scaleway | France (groupe Iliad) | Paris, Varsovie | H100 2,87 €, L40S 1,47 €, L4 0,79 € | facturé à la minute |
| Infomaniak | Suisse | Suisse | A100 80 Go 1,31 €, L40S 0,63 €, L4 0,25 € | instance complète ; GPU activés sur demande |
| Nebius | Pays-Bas (Amsterdam) | Finlande, France, Madrid, Royaume-Uni | H100 3,85 $, H200 4,50 $, L40S dès 1,55 $ | hausse annoncée au 1er octobre 2026 (H100 à 4,50 $) |
| Verda (ex-DataCrunch) | Finlande | Helsinki | H100 3,56 $, A100 80 Go 1,80 $, L40S 1,54 $ | facturé par tranches prépayées de 10 minutes |

Les spécialistes du calcul, Nebius et Verda, louent surtout des H100 et H200, facturées en dollars, depuis des datacenters nordiques. Et les offres de niche : Outscale pour les administrations qui exigent SecNumCloud, IONOS pour la seule H200 de Francfort, Hetzner pour qui préfère louer un serveur au mois.

Here is where the market sits as of November 14, 2026, measured across 527 live offers from 38 providers for 65 distinct GPUs. The numbers below are the cheapest on-demand or community rate we can find for each card, read from the live market each time this page loads, which is the price you could actually rent at today, not a list price or an average. Every figure links to its live page, where the provider behind the floor and every other offer for the card are listed.

The shape of the snapshot is a steep curve from commodity to flagship. Among the commodity cards, the RTX 4090 rents from $0.14 an hour and the L4 from $0.11, genuinely pocket-change compute for small inference and image generation. Among the workhorses, the A100 80GB sits at $0.52 and the H100 SXM at $1.73. At the top, the newest, largest-memory parts command a premium for their memory and throughput: the H200 at $2.50, the B200 at $4.89 (141GB and 180GB of HBM3e respectively - NVIDIA's H200 and DGX B200 pages), and the B300 at $5.89. The AMD MI300X, with a huge 192GB of memory - AMD ROCm docs, rents from $1.71, which is why it keeps appearing in large-model inference plans despite the software friction of leaving CUDA.

The reason the curve is worth reading closely is that each rung maps to a class of work, and paying for a higher rung than your workload needs is the most common way to burn money. The bottom rung, the RTX 4090 at $0.14 and the L4 at $0.11, comfortably runs small-model inference, image generation, and quantized 7B-to-13B language models, which is the bulk of real production traffic. The middle rung, the A100 at $0.31 (40GB) and $0.52 (80GB), handles 70B inference at reduced precision and mid-size fine-tuning.

...

Beyond the four charted cards, the same split held across the wider catalog. The A100 40GB floor was flat to the cent for the entire window, the steadiest price on the board, and the L40S and A6000 held tight ranges. At the other extreme, the H200 floor swung about 16% and the MI300X about 13%, both on thin liquidity, so their "floor" is really the cheapest of a handful of listings that appear and disappear. Thin supply, not a genuine trend, is what makes a new or niche card's price look jumpy, and it is worth remembering before reading a large weekly move on a low-liquidity card as a market signal rather than an artifact of a single host changing its rate.

...

The consistent floor-setter in our data has been the marketplace model. In the study window, Vast.ai held the cheapest rate for a striking number of cards, including the A100 80GB at $0.54, the A100 40GB at $0.27, and the RTX 4090 at $0.14, because its third-party hosts set prices by supply and demand with almost no overhead - Vast.ai. As of November 14, 2026, the A100 80GB floor is held by Vast.ai at $0.52, the A100 40GB floor by Vast.ai at $0.31, and the RTX 4090 floor by Vast.ai at $0.14. RunPod listed the broadest catalog we saw in the study, 30 distinct GPUs spanning community and on-demand tiers, which made it the practical first stop for availability. Note how far the floor sits below the advertised neocloud rate for the same card: the cheapest guaranteed H100 in our data is $1.73 from Vast.ai right now, while the larger neoclouds publish $3.20 (Hyperstack) and $3.99 (Lambda) for their H100 SXM - Lambda. On the newest silicon the floor shifted to specialist neoclouds in the study, with DeepInfra holding the cheapest B200 and B300 on-demand rates; as of November 14, 2026, those floors belong to DeepInfra ( $4.89) and DeepInfra ( $5.89).

results.title: The same GPU, at very different prices · infratoapp
highlights:
The median gap between the cheapest and dearest seller of an identical card is 3.8×. The widest is the V100-16GB: $0.24 per GPU-hour at Verda (DataCrunch) against $2.85 at Runcrate, a gap of 11.8×. An H100 SXM 80GB — the card most of this market is actually built on — runs from $2.16 to $6.16 across 13 sellers, a gap of 2.8×.

These are headline on-demand rates, before any commitment discount, for the same part. Not a similar part, not a different memory configuration, and not one region against another.
